questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut copies the selected item to the clipboard?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C copies the selection without removing it from its original location.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut pastes the contents of the clipboard?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+V inserts whatever was last copied or cut to the clipboard.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut cuts the selected item?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+X removes the selection and places it on the clipboard for pasting.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut undoes the last action?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Z reverses the most recent change in most applications.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut redoes a previously undone action?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Y reapplies an action that was undone with Ctrl+Z.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut selects all items or all text?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+A highlights everything in the current document or window.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut saves the current document?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S writes the current document to disk in most applications.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens the print dialog?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+P is the standard print shortcut across Windows applications and browsers.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens the find or search box in most applications?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+F opens a search box to locate text within the current page or document.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut cycles through open applications in Windows?
questions.explanation: Holding Alt and pressing Tab switches between currently running programs.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut closes the active window or quits the application?
questions.explanation: Alt+F4 closes the focused window and, on the desktop, opens the shutdown dialog.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens Task Manager directly in Windows?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+Esc launches Task Manager immediately without an intermediate menu.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut locks your Windows computer?
questions.explanation: Win+L instantly locks the session, requiring a password to resume.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer in Windows?
questions.explanation: Win+E launches File Explorer so you can browse files and folders.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut shows the desktop in Windows?
questions.explanation: Win+D toggles all windows minimized to reveal the desktop.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens a new tab in most web browsers?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+T opens a new tab; Ctrl+N opens a whole new browser window instead.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut reopens the last closed browser tab?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+T restores recently closed tabs, including their history.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut bookmarks the current page in most browsers?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+D saves the current page to bookmarks or favorites.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut jumps the cursor to the browser's address bar?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+L highlights the address bar so you can type a URL or search term.

questions.question: Which key refreshes or reloads a web page?
questions.explanation: F5 reloads the page; Ctrl+F5 forces a reload bypassing the cache.

questions.question: Which key renames a selected file in File Explorer?
questions.explanation: F2 puts the selected file's name into edit mode for renaming.

questions.question: Which key toggles full-screen mode in browsers and most media players?
questions.explanation: F11 expands the window to fill the entire screen, hiding toolbars.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut makes selected text bold in most editors?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+B toggles bold formatting in word processors and rich text fields.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut snaps the active window to the left half of the screen?
questions.explanation: Win+Left arrow docks the window to the left side for split-screen multitasking.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Run dialog in Windows?
questions.explanation: Win+R opens the Run box for launching programs or system tools by name.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut moves the cursor to the beginning of a document?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Home jumps to the very top of a document, while Home alone goes to line start.
